stem:
Alok draws two angles on paper. Angle $M$ has short arms and a wide turn about its vertex. Angle $N$ has long arms and a narrow turn about its vertex.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims correctly decide which angle is larger?

options.text: Angle $M$ is larger, because it has the greater amount of turn about the vertex.
Angle $N$ is larger, because its arms are drawn longer.
Arm length does not decide size when the amount of turn is what is compared.
Angle $M$ and angle $N$ have the same size on Alok's paper.

teacher.key_rationale: Angle size is the amount of turn about the vertex, so M is larger and arm length does not decide size. Saying longer arms make N larger reverses the size relation. Claiming equal size on the paper omits comparing the turns.
